title: How to Build an Adaptive AI Tutor for Any Course Using Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a core problem in AI tutoring systems: large language models can produce factually incorrect answers and often fail to preserve conceptual relationships between course ideas. The authors argue that standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), while improving factual grounding, still relies mainly on semantic similarity and therefore can miss the structured links that matter in education.

To address this, the paper proposes KG-RAG, an adaptive AI tutor framework that combines a large language model (DeepSeek-V3), retrieval-augmented generation, and a knowledge graph built from course materials. The knowledge graph is constructed by automatically extracting entities and relationships from lecture content and then validating them with a domain expert. During question answering, the system expands retrieval through graph traversal so that responses include related concepts as well as directly relevant text.

The empirical study involved 76 first-year university students with no prior finance coursework. Students were randomly assigned to either a standard RAG tutor or the KG-RAG tutor, used the system during a 45-minute session after a 3-hour self-study period, and then completed a multiple-choice assessment. The KG-RAG group scored significantly higher than the RAG group, and student feedback also suggested improved relevance, usability, and understanding. The paper concludes that knowledge-graph-enhanced retrieval can improve the completeness, precision, and relational coherence of AI tutor responses, leading to better learning outcomes in higher education settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a controlled experiment with random assignment to KG-RAG versus standard RAG, which supports causal inference, but it is a small single-site study with a narrow finance-course context and limited evidence of broader external validity. The paper also includes user feedback, but the main learning outcome evidence comes from one modest RCT-like comparison.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported learning gain is large for the general student sample (Cohen's d=0.86), well above the threshold for blue impact. Although the setting is specific, the magnitude suggests substantial potential educational impact if replicated.

interventions.use_case: Knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation tutoring system for university course Q&A, using DeepSeek-V3 to answer student questions with structured course knowledge and context-aware explanations.
Adaptive AI tutor architecture that combines LLM generation, RAG, and knowledge-graph retrieval to deliver personalized instructional responses and support self-study.

finding.finding_summary: In a controlled experiment with n=76 first-year university students, KG-RAG produced higher post-interaction assessment scores than standard RAG. The KG-RAG group scored M=6.37 (SD=1.92) versus M=4.71 (SD=1.93) on a 10-point quiz, with t=-3.75, p=0.00035, and a large effect size (Cohen's d=0.86).
finding.measure: 10-point multiple-choice assessment of finance course knowledge after a 3-hour self-study period and 45-minute tutoring session
